items.headline: Trump publicly rejects Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap, expects to resume bombing after midterms
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported (confirmed by CNBC, Al Jazeera, CNN and NPR) that Trump rejected a formal seven-day roadmap Iran submitted via Qatari mediators on Fri 25 Sep -- a phased plan running from a regional ceasefire to Hormuz reopening to resumed nuclear talks. Trump called it 'not acceptable,' said Iran is 'losing so badly,' and told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November US midterms. Al Jazeera's correspondent described the roadmap as 'dead in the water.'
items.actionable: This reverses Friday's truce-hope framing -- expect Monday's Asia open to price renewed war-premium risk, not de-escalation; keep the silver/gold-miner sleeve sized for escalation into the ~Mon-Tue deadline rather than a quiet rollover.

items.headline: Oil reverses higher after Trump's rejection headline; Hormuz traffic still 'at a standstill'
items.summary: Following Trump's rejection of Iran's roadmap, Brent moved back toward ~$103/bbl (+~2%) and WTI toward ~$97/bbl (+~1.5%), unwinding Friday's truce-hope-driven pullback, as reports described shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as still at a standstill. Saudi Aramco's CEO was quoted separately calling the ongoing supply disruption 'the largest the world has ever experienced.'
items.actionable: The real-yield headwind that pressured gold/silver miners Friday may be partly offset by a firmer war-premium bid into Monday -- don't extrapolate Friday's oil pullback into this week.

items.headline: Bitcoin drops ~3.8% then partly recovers on Iran-rejection headline; ~$255M in crypto liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell from a run toward $87,000 to roughly $83,900 within hours of the WSJ report on Trump's rejection breaking Saturday, before recovering to around $84,000. Crypto-wide liquidations hit approximately $255M on 26 Sep, with BTC accounting for about $63M of that; no BTC-specific regulatory or ETF catalyst was identified -- the move was driven entirely by the Iran headline.
items.actionable: Crypto was the only market open and reacted first to the Iran escalation -- a preview of the risk-off impulse that could hit equities/HK tech at Monday's open if the deadline lapses without a deal.

items.headline: Iran says it awaits a 'formal' US response, hasn't declared the Hormuz deadline void
items.summary: Iranian FM Araghchi said Sunday that Tehran has 'noted' Trump's public rejection but is still awaiting a formal US response via Qatari mediators before deciding next steps. The ultimatum (issued 24 Sep, expiring roughly Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) has not been formally withdrawn by either side, but the core terms -- a naval-blockade lift, frozen-asset release, sanctions waiver and regional ceasefire -- appear to have been rejected by the US.
items.actionable: The deadline is not confirmed lapsed, but the tone from both sides points toward a binary, volatile resolution early this week rather than a quiet rollover -- watch Monday/Tuesday closely for the next concrete step.

items.headline: Planned Iran-Gulf-states meeting on Hormuz terms postponed over the weekend
items.summary: A separate meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states intended to discuss Strait of Hormuz terms was postponed over the weekend, removing what had been seen as a secondary step toward easing shipping disruption, alongside Trump's rejection of Iran's main roadmap.
items.actionable: Removes a near-term de-escalation pathway, reinforcing the case that the ultimatum deadline passes this week without resolution.

items.headline: Wall Street closes hawkish week with a rally as 10-year yield hits post-2008 high
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow gained 0.93% to 51,828.62 (snapping a three-week losing streak), and the Nasdaq added ~0.48% to 27,068.72 on Friday, with all three posting weekly gains despite the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 5.18%, its highest since the 2008 financial crisis. VIX eased to ~14.9 even as the bond selloff continued.
items.actionable: Equities shrugging off 5%+ yields is a near-term risk-on tell, but with the weekend's Iran escalation on top, the yield/geopolitics combination still favors keeping the cash pile large rather than chasing the rally.

items.headline: BofA Flow Show: global equity funds swing to outflow as US leads the reversal
items.summary: BofA's weekly Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep 2026) showed US equity funds losing $21.1bn and global equity funds losing a net $10.2bn -- a sharp reversal from the prior week's +$63.8bn US equity inflow (the best week in three months). Fixed income kept its 74-week inflow streak alive (+$17.3bn); the Bull & Bear Indicator eased to 9.3, still in the contrarian 'Sell' zone. As of a Sunday recheck, the regional/gold/money-market sub-split for this specific week still has not been published.
items.actionable: A one-week swing from the best equity-inflow week in three months to an outright outflow is an early tell that positioning is reacting to the hawkish Fed -- a reason not to read Friday's index rally as confirmation the flow backdrop has turned durably risk-on.

items.headline: Gold and silver pull back on stronger dollar and higher real yields
items.summary: Gold closed around $4,265/oz (down roughly 0.5-0.6%) and silver around $63.5/oz (down roughly 1.1-1.4%) on Friday as a firmer US dollar and rising real yields (10-year nominal at 5.18%) outweighed safe-haven demand. The weekend's Iran-Hormuz escalation (Trump's roadmap rejection, postponed Gulf-states meeting) is a fresh, partially offsetting tailwind not yet reflected in Friday's close.
items.actionable: Rising real yields remain the dominant near-term headwind for the levered silver/gold-miner book, but watch whether the weekend's renewed war premium offsets it at Monday's open -- the two forces are now pulling in opposite directions.

items.headline: Week ahead: September payrolls due Friday, consensus roughly halving to ~85k
items.summary: The week of 28 Sep-2 Oct brings PCE and Dallas Fed manufacturing data Monday, Q2 GDP final and jobless claims mid-week, ISM Manufacturing PMI Thursday, and September nonfarm payrolls Friday 2 Oct with consensus around 85k, roughly half August's 162k. A heavy Fed-speaker calendar continues, and the 30-year mortgage rate sits at a 2-year high (~7.45%). No FOMC minutes this week (due ~8 Oct for the 16 Sep meeting).
items.actionable: Friday's payrolls print is the key swing factor for whether the Fed's hawkish path holds -- a soft number would cut against the 'further hikes' narrative embedded in the model's bond calls.

items.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub and a Riyadh target; six missiles intercepted
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on a target in Riyadh and Aramco facilities at the Red Sea port of Yanbu on 25 September; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted six ballistic missiles, with no confirmed damage or casualties. Aramco supplies roughly 10% of global oil demand.
items.actionable: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, now compounded by the weekend's diplomatic breakdown, keep the oil-shock/inflation-hedge case for gold-silver miners intact.

items.headline: US-China critical-minerals talks end without a concrete deal; magnet flows still 'not up to par'
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent and USTR Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York the week of 21 September for preparatory talks covering AI safety guardrails, the tariff-truce extension, and rare-earth magnet flows, concluding around Trump-Xi's 24 September Washington meeting with no public outcome or new deadline announced. A senior US official said China's mineral-flow restoration has underperformed expectations, consistent with the 21% month-on-month drop in Chinese rare-earth magnet exports to the US in August.
items.actionable: Persistently constrained Chinese magnet exports with no resolution keeps the structural bull case for the rare-earth watchlist (MP Materials, Lynas, USA Rare Earth) intact; JL Mag (6680.HK) is more exposed to any China-side demand slowdown.

items.headline: Hang Seng slips 1% in thin trade as tech and property drag
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index closed down 1.01% at 24,510.09 and the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.13% to 4,311.78 on Friday, with Xiaomi (-2.6%), NetEase (-3.1%) and property developers lower. Mainland China markets (and Southbound Stock Connect) were then closed 25-27 Sep for the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, resuming Monday 28 Sep -- so no fresh HK/Southbound read is available until then.
items.actionable: Weak Friday follow-through plus the mainland holiday closure argues for staying selective in 0700/0981/1810 into Monday's reopen rather than adding broad beta ahead of the Iran-deadline binary risk.

items.headline: Jefferies initiates Singapore banks: Buy DBS and UOB, Hold OCBC
items.summary: Jefferies started coverage citing the banks' proven resilience across credit cycles, superior capital generation, and further scope for earnings/dividend compounding, with OCBC initiated at Hold (the lowest rating of the three). The call comes as rising SORA following the Fed hike is seen restoring net interest margins after years of compression.
items.actionable: Fresh sell-side conviction on DBS/UOB reinforces the case that the Singapore bank leg is a direct beneficiary of the same hawkish Fed pivot pressuring the silver/gold miners leg -- a natural internal hedge within the portfolio.

note: Sunday catch-up run, 27 Sep 2026 07:02 SGT. All markets remain closed for the weekend; the latest completed cash sessions are Fri 25 Sep (US/HK/SG) and 23 Sep (KRX, closed for Chuseok through 27 Sep, reopens Mon 28 Sep). The dominant development is a genuine weekend escalation: Trump publicly rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap on Sat 26 Sep and a planned Iran-Gulf-states meeting was postponed, reversing Friday's truce-hope framing; oil gapped higher into Sunday's Globex reopen and Bitcoin (the only market trading through the weekend) fell then partly recovered on the headline. 5 of the 13 items above (26/26/26/26/27 Sep) are within the last 24-48 hours, comfortably meeting the freshness requirement. Congress/insider filings were actively checked for the weekend window and none were found, as expected since STOCK Act filers, SGX, HKEX and EDGAR do not process weekend filings.
